declaredConfiguration.name: spawn
declaredConfiguration.description: Owned child source; guard parent-only top-level work with isProcessChild for self-spawn.

declaredConfiguration.name: connect
declaredConfiguration.description: Borrow the external process and own only the dialed local session.

declaredConfiguration.name: listen
declaredConfiguration.description: Own a listener and accepted sessions, without launching a process.

declaredConfiguration.name: report
declaredConfiguration.description: Optional diagnostics sink; omission uses Core's defaultRpcReporter.

declaredConfiguration.name: endpointFactory
declaredConfiguration.description: A custom runtime assembly receives only the operations held by this channel view.

declaredConfiguration.name: self
declaredConfiguration.description: Optional local identity; omission generates an instance id with the display name peer.

declaredConfiguration.name: provide
declaredConfiguration.description: Explicit nested own-data method groups; defaults to no application methods and rejects * accessors during compilation.

declaredConfiguration.name: providerLimits
declaredConfiguration.description: Provider quotas, defaulting to 256 global and 64 per verified peer.

declaredConfiguration.name: authentication
declaredConfiguration.description: Existing per-frame credentials enable signed native transfer without a custom endpoint.

declaredConfiguration.name: probe
declaredConfiguration.description: Installs an endpoint-local synchronous observer without changing pipeline selection.

declaredConfiguration.name: defaultTimeoutMs
declaredConfiguration.description: Only request/stream inherit this positive default in their original timeout scope.

declaredConfiguration.name: contract
declaredConfiguration.description: Explicit advanced schema, modes and idempotency retain their original contract owner.

declaredConfiguration.name: keyFactory
declaredConfiguration.description: Optional idempotency key generator; omission uses the canonical identity generator.

declaredConfiguration.name: retryPort
declaredConfiguration.description: Optional whole-invocation retry policy; omission sends once.

declaredConfiguration.name: token
declaredConfiguration.description: Credential for explicit addresses; same-user Unix named endpoints have an OS-isolated default.

declaredConfiguration.name: verify
declaredConfiguration.description: Optional listener verifier; omission compares the configured token and returns the local principal.

options: Usually the same `spawn` / `connect` / `listen` / `provide` as `createProcessPeer`, plus `name` and optional `expose`; or a full `IProcessPluginOptions`.
A plugin for `host.use()`.
name: Caller-selected nonempty registration name copied when constructing the cold plugin; use the same name when addressing host.process.
Use the application-owned value shown here when configuring this connection. Omitted optional values keep their documented defaults.
contract: Application remote contract. Required and matched to name for a full deployment; optional for runtime sources, where provide normally supplies the directory.
Omitted: provided method definitions supply the normal inferred runtime directory.
registrationOwner: Identifies the plugin registration that may be removed if its process cannot recover. In the full deployment form, supply the exact registration name and the Host that installs it. When failure reports remain unhandled, cleanup uses this Host to remove that registration. The name must equal options.name and the Host must provide unUse; missing or mismatched values reject configuration before process setup.
resilience: Caller-owned governance from createProcessResilience, borrowed by this plugin rather than closed with it.
Omitted: create and own a governor using the deployment scheduler and report callback.
host: Full deployment: Host port owning installation and replacement. Runtime form: the actual installing Host, needed only when exposing host control with catalog and resolvePlugin.
Omitted: allowed unless expose contains host; explicit host exposure requires host, catalog and resolvePlugin together.
endpointFactory: Endpoint factory called with the acquired channel and abort signal; mandatory for full deployments, while runtime sources can use canonical endpoint assembly.
endpointFactory.channel: IRemoteChannelResources acquired by the selected platform source; ownership remains with the original construction.
endpointFactory.signal: Native construction cancellation signal supplied by the peer owner.
Promise of the endpoint assembled for this exact channel; throw or rejection preserves the original construction failure.
Required in the full deployment overload; no endpoint factory is inferred.
Build the explicit full-deployment endpoint from this acquired channel; retain its pipeline and flow-control features.
report: Receives background errors that no call can reject with.
report.error: Original background failure value; preserve its source and code when present.
Nothing; the error is reported.
`defaultRpcReporter`, which reports through the default console path.
Route native process and background diagnostics to the application sink without printing credentials.
keyFactory: Key callback for automatically keyed idempotent calls in full deployments and managed runtime spawn/connect bindings. Function sources use direct Core assembly and do not consume it.
Application-issued string key for that call.
Omitted: the proxy uses defaultRpcId.
Managed process spawn/connect consumes this policy for declared idempotent requests. A function source uses direct Core assembly and does not consume this proxy policy.
retryPort: Whole-invocation dispatch port for full deployments and managed runtime spawn/connect bindings. Function sources use the direct Core call path.
Omitted: createRemoteRetryPort uses the binding events, scheduler and reporter.
deployment: Spawn or connect deployment.
self: Application-supplied safe identity with nonempty name and instanceId; neither credentials nor arbitrary properties are published.
Omitted: the core uses RUNTIME_PEER_DEFAULT_NAME and a generated defaultRpcId; trusted platform bootstrap may supply its own identity.
provide: Application-provided local methods, descriptors or allowed runtime forwarding entries compiled into the accepted directory; methods receive the remote payload and preserve synchronous or async failures.
Omitted: this side publishes no application methods.
providerLimits: Provider admission policy forwarded to the canonical endpoint; it does not alter transport framing or acquire another provider registry.
Omitted: the original endpoint or listener admission owner supplies its standard provider limits.
authentication: Original signing, verification and optional encryption configuration installed into canonical endpoint assembly; invalid credentials reject construction before publication.

probe: One IRpcProbe or an array of probes from the application, installed as endpoint-local synchronous observers without selecting a different pipeline.
Omitted: no observer is added by this field.
defaultTimeoutMs: Finite positive millisecond default for request and stream calls, validated before acquiring source resources; it does not extend the notify or group timeout scope.
30000 ms for request and stream in the original timeout scope.
spawn: Child to start and own: `URL`, path (relative to the main entry directory), `true` (current entry), a short object `{ entry | command, args?, wrap?, wire?, ... }`, or a full `ISpawnProcessPluginDeployment`.
Not set.
connect: Running service to dial: a name (`math-service`), `tcp://127.0.0.1:port`, a Unix path, or a full connect deployment.
listen: Address or name to accept sessions on; each session is its own connection.
token: Shared secret checked in the handshake; required for TCP, explicit socket paths and Windows pipes. Generate it per deployment and never log it.
Not set: named endpoints rely on OS user permissions.
verify: Listener side: `(auth, peer) => principalId` validating the client credential; throw to reject.
verify.auth: Portable credential from the incoming handshake, possibly undefined.
verify.peer: Handshake peer metadata supplied by the accepted transport.
Verified principal string or its Promise; throw or rejection refuses the candidate.
Not set: the `token` comparison is used.
Require an application principal for a listener rather than relying only on same-user socket permissions.
connectTimeoutMs: How long a named `connect` waits for the listener to appear.
`5000`.
expose: Distinct nonempty paths explicitly exposing current Host feature methods, runtime connection routes or the reserved host control entry. Only this snapshotted whitelist becomes remotely callable.
Omitted: an empty whitelist; only provide methods are published.
catalog: Application-authored IRemoteHostCatalog declaring the only plugin contracts available through explicitly exposed host control.
Omitted: no host-control catalog; required when expose contains host.
resolvePlugin: Synchronous local resolver invoked by the canonical host-control owner after catalog admission; definitions remain local and are installed through the original Host.
resolvePlugin.name: Plugin name admitted by the declared catalog.
resolvePlugin.config: Optional portable configuration from the remote host-use request.
Local plugin definition accepted by the Host; a thrown error rejects the host-use request.
Omitted: no local resolver; required when expose contains host.
Resolve only catalog-admitted names to local definitions when host is explicitly exposed.
registrationOwner.name: Names the one registration that failure cleanup may remove. Set it to the value of options.name for this plugin before constructing the full deployment. A different name rejects configuration, preventing failure handling for this plugin from removing another registration.
registrationOwner.host: Supplies the Host that actually installs this plugin. Failure cleanup invokes its unUse method to remove the named registration and apply the Host rules for dependent plugins. Pass that original Host; an object without unUse is rejected before process setup. The caller continues to own the Host.

symbols.purpose: Establishes a raw byte channel with its explicit handshake policy, or a message channel with matching static profiles; used in establish of full sources.
symbols.core:
channel: Raw channel from a launcher handle, `dialProcessByteChannel` or stdio.
options: `IProcessByteOptions`: `role`, `offer`, `peerId`, `auth` (responder), `scheduler`, `signal`, `ipc`, `report`.
The established channel; bad credentials throw `PROCESS_CHANNEL_AUTH_REJECTED`, slow handshakes `PROCESS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT`.
peerId: Caller-selected remote routing identity, usually from the launched process or received bootstrap; a negotiated runtime identity may supersede it.
Use the application-owned value shown here when configuring this connection. Omitted optional values keep their documented defaults.
signal: Caller-owned IAbortSignal cancelling this handshake attempt; later connection ownership remains with the returned channel.
Omitted: no external abort listener is attached.
handshakeTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative handshake budget in milliseconds; expiration rejects with PROCESS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT.
10000 ms for the Core byte or message handshake.
scheduler: Caller-selected IScheduler providing monotonic time and handshake timers, forwarded to the established endpoint.
Core systemScheduler.
report: Receives background errors that no call can reject with.
report.error: Original background failure value; preserve its source and code when present.
Nothing; the error is reported.
Send secondary failures to the application diagnostic sink while preserving the original error identity.
ipc: Caller-authored connection and session labels plus the logging port; stderr and queue limits are optional.
Correlate connection records and configure queue capacity without treating diagnostic labels as credentials.
role: Explicit local handshake role: initiator sends an offer, while responder supplies both an offer and an authentication decision.
Start the byte handshake using this side’s explicit offer.
Answer the byte handshake and enforce the declared auth policy.
Use initiator on the dialing or launching side and responder on the byte receiver; both sides supply an offer.
offer: Local `IRpcHandshakeOffer` returned by the selected offer preparation helper or authored from `@migaia/rpc-contract` policy; both roles must supply it.
auth: Responder-only authentication union: mode required invokes `verify(auth, peer)` with portable credentials and handshake peer metadata; return a principal string or void, synchronously or asynchronously. Throw/rejection refuses the handshake. Mode none explicitly skips authentication.
auth.auth: Portable credential value received from the initiator, possibly undefined.
auth.peer: Peer metadata supplied by the handshake boundary from `@migaia/rpc-contract`.
Verified principal string or void, optionally promised; a failure rejects the handshake.
Require verification on externally reachable byte channels; select none only when the carrier is already private and owned.
staticAgreement: Fixed capabilities agreed by both sides (no negotiation).
ipc.connectionId: Caller-issued non-secret identifier for this physical connection, copied into diagnostic records.
ipc.sessionId: Caller-issued identifier for this logical session, allowing records from one session to be correlated.
ipc.processId: Optional process label issued by the caller for diagnostic correlation; it grants no authentication authority.
Omitted: records have no process label.
ipc.maxPendingData: Maximum queued data frames in the canonical Core send queue; separate control capacity remains available.
256 pending data frames.
ipc.maxPendingControl: Maximum queued control frames in the canonical Core send queue, independent of data-frame capacity.
8 pending control frames.
ipc.log: Callback receiving each Core IIpcLogRecord; synchronous throws and Promise rejections enter the original reporter boundary.
ipc.log.record: Structured, connection-labelled IPC record supplied by Core.
Void or Promise<void>; asynchronous completion is observed by the logging owner.
Collect structured connection records; keep secret bytes out of the sink and let report observe sink failures.
ipc.stderr: Subscription callback for child stderr bytes. The diagnostic bridge records bounded redacted summaries rather than the raw text.
ipc.stderr.listener: Bridge callback receiving each Uint8Array chunk from the child.
Unsubscribe function owned and invoked by the connection cleanup.
Omitted: no child-stderr subscription is attached.
Borrow the existing child stderr subscription for bounded redacted diagnostics and unsubscribe during channel cleanup.
auth.mode: Explicit responder authentication policy; initiator options carry no auth decision object.
Verify initiator credentials and reject throw or rejection.
Explicitly perform the handshake without credential verification.
Choose required for credential verification; none explicitly omits verification on an already private carrier.
auth.verify: Required-mode responder callback receiving remote portable auth and IRpcPeerInfo; return a principal string or void, synchronously or by Promise. Failure rejects authentication.
auth.verify.auth: Portable credential value received from the initiator, possibly undefined.
auth.verify.peer: Peer metadata supplied by the handshake boundary from `@migaia/rpc-contract`.
staticAgreement.local: Caller-authored local static message profile, declared before any message transport activation.
staticAgreement.peer: Caller-authored expected peer profile; codec and capability order must exactly match the local profile.
staticAgreement.local.codec: This transport already delivers complete messages. Set the local codec to identity, which passes native message values through without converting them to bytes. A byte codec is rejected during configuration, before the transport is activated.
Sends each original message value unchanged. Choose identity for the local side because the underlying transport already preserves message boundaries.
Use identity on both profiles when the native carrier already preserves complete messages.
staticAgreement.local.capabilities: Lists the communication capabilities this local endpoint declares, in their fixed order. Use the same entries and order in the expected peer profile. This complete-message path does not negotiate a different list during setup.
staticAgreement.peer.codec: Set the expected peer codec to identity as well, meaning the peer sends message values without byte encoding. A different peer codec cannot match this complete-message transport and is rejected during configuration.
Requires the peer to send unchanged message values too. This matches the local format; a byte-encoded peer format would not match.
staticAgreement.peer.capabilities: Lists the capabilities expected from the peer. Every entry and its position must match the local list. If a capability is missing or differently ordered, this message-transport path cannot negotiate a correction.

peerId: Caller-selected remote routing identity, usually from the launched process or received bootstrap; a negotiated runtime identity may supersede it.
Use the application-owned value shown here when configuring this connection. Omitted optional values keep their documented defaults.
signal: Caller-owned IAbortSignal cancelling this handshake attempt; later connection ownership remains with the returned channel.
Omitted: no external abort listener is attached.
handshakeTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative millisecond budget for the initial JSON-RPC bridge handshake; it does not bound later method calls.
10000 ms from JsonRpcLimit.handshakeMs.
scheduler: Required caller-selected IScheduler for handshake deadline and established connection tasks; no clock is inferred by this bridge.
report: Receives background errors that no call can reject with.
report.error: Original background failure value; preserve its source and code when present.
Nothing; the error is reported.
Send secondary failures to the application diagnostic sink while preserving the original error identity.
ipc: Caller-authored connection and session labels plus the logging port; stderr and queue limits are optional.
Correlate connection records and configure queue capacity without treating diagnostic labels as credentials.
byte: Caller-owned ordered IProcessByteChannel returned by a launcher, socket adapter or stdio wrapper, with kind byte.
target: Explicit plugin contract or host catalog target: plugin requires contract only, while host requires catalog only. Stream declarations are rejected.
offer: Caller-authored native offer without auth or codecs. The bridge inserts the token, JSON codec and required JSON-RPC capabilities.
token: Nonempty credential issued by the deployment owner and expected by the JSON-RPC peer; copied into the bridge handshake, never diagnostic output.
wallClock: Required caller-selected IWallClock supplying timestamp() for outgoing JSON-RPC message sentAt metadata, distinct from monotonic scheduling.

sections.content: Import IProcessPluginDescriptor from @migaia/rpc-process, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use IProcessPluginDescriptor when its type contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when IProcessPluginDescriptor does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained type example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
descriptorVersion: Required descriptor schema version, currently the literal 1; parser rejects unsupported versions.
Use the current strict process descriptor schema.
target: Descriptor discriminant choosing the plugin contract branch or the remote host catalog branch.
Describe one plugin with a required contract and optional instance mode.
Describe a remote host with its required exported catalog.
name: Caller-issued remote registration name validated against the canonical remote-name grammar.
runtime: Caller-selected runtime adapter name retained in the portable descriptor for materialization.
deployment: Pure-data `IProcessPluginDeploymentDescriptor` selecting spawned byte/message deployment or a borrowed external connection.
instanceMode: Plugin-only `ProcessPluginInstanceMode` deciding shared or per-connection exposure; host descriptors reject this field.
Omitted: parser preserves absence for the materialization policy to resolve.
Share the plugin instance across its accepted connections.
Select connection-specific plugin instance ownership.
replaceStrategy: Optional whole-process replacement strategy for spawned deployment: stop-then-start or start-then-switch. Connect deployments reject it.
Omitted: parser does not add a replacement strategy.
Stop the current generation before starting its replacement.
Prepare a new process candidate before switching the host registration.
contract: Required plugin-only `IRemoteContract` describing callable Feature methods; host descriptors use catalog instead.
catalog: Required host-only `IRemoteHostCatalog` describing the exported remote host capabilities.

sections.title: 高阶用法
sections.content: Validate persisted pure-data deployment descriptions before choosing runtime adapters and materializing a plugin or host.

symbols.core:
name: Plugin name in the host.
Configure this part of the advanced pricing deployment.
contract: Declared remote methods.
registrationOwner: Identifies the plugin registration that may be removed if its process cannot recover. In the full deployment form, supply the exact registration name and the Host that installs it. When failure reports remain unhandled, cleanup uses this Host to remove that registration. The name must equal options.name and the Host must provide unUse; missing or mismatched values reject configuration before process setup.
resilience: Caller-owned governance from createProcessResilience, borrowed by this plugin rather than closed with it.
Omitted: create and own a governor using the deployment scheduler and report callback.
host: Host port used to install and replace the plugin.
endpointFactory: Advanced synchronous invocation of an async endpoint factory with this acquired channel and native abort signal; its Promise must resolve an IRemoteServeEndpoint. Failure triggers construction rollback.
endpointFactory.channel: IRemoteChannelResources acquired by the selected platform source; ownership remains with the original construction.
endpointFactory.signal: Native construction cancellation signal supplied by the peer owner.
Promise of the endpoint assembled for this exact channel; throw or rejection preserves the original construction failure.
Required in the full deployment overload; no endpoint factory is inferred.
Build the explicit full-deployment endpoint from this acquired channel; retain its pipeline and flow-control features.
report: Receives background errors that no call can reject with.
report.error: Original background failure value; preserve its source and code when present.
Nothing; the error is reported.
Send secondary failures to the application diagnostic sink while preserving the original error identity.
keyFactory: Synchronous callback returning an idempotency key when the full deployment remote proxy automatically keys an idempotent call.
Application-issued string key for that call.
Omitted: the proxy uses defaultRpcId.
Issue an application key for a declared idempotent proxy call when the caller supplies no explicit key.
retryPort: Caller-provided IRemoteRetryPort dispatching full-deployment proxy retries through the original binding.
Omitted: createRemoteRetryPort uses the binding events, scheduler and reporter.
deployment: Spawn or connect deployment.

symbols.purpose: Governance owner returned by `createProcessResilience()`. The [terminal-child case](/en/docs/rpc-process/api/createProcessResilience#rpc-process-index--createProcessResilience--case-2) shows how to attach the original supervisor and release its resources separately; the factory example introduces the required dependencies and policies.
symbols.core:
sessionOptions: Builds result-deduplication settings and call limits for one accepted session. Result deduplication lets retries of an identified operation reuse its stored outcome. Pass the session identity received by listenRegistrations; its listener example below shows how to obtain that identity.
sessionOptions.identity: `{ connectionId, sessionId, principalId, processId? }`: accepted connection labels; principalId must be a nonempty verified principal. processId defaults to undefined. This method derives options and does not authenticate. The returned scope accepts { token, senderId }, but partitions by principalId under this governor.
`{ idempotency, limits }`.
listenRegistrations: Accepts registrations of remote processes on an address.
listenRegistrations.options: `IProcessRegistrationListenOptions`.
A listener with `address` and `close()`.
attachRegistration: Registers a supervised process with this failure-management object. The supervisor starts and restarts the process; this registration adds reporting and eventual removal if recovery fails. Supply the binding and cleanup owner shown in the complete usage example above.
attachRegistration.name: Registration name, the plugin `name`.
attachRegistration.binding: `ownership` is spawn-owned or connection-borrowed; `health` is ping, custom or none; both are required. supervisor supplies restart(), inspect(), dispose() and onTerminal(listener). The example forwards methods to the original process supervisor.
attachRegistration.liquidation: Required owner union: standalone-host supplies release(): Promise<void>; proxy-plugin supplies the same registration name and actual Host with unUse. It runs on liquidation, not ordinary registration.close().
An `IProcessRegistration`.
callGuard: Returns a stable check for this registration: terminal state refuses new calls, and liquidation keeps refusing them through the retained diagnostic record. Run guard.beforeDispatch() before each dispatch; bypassing it skips this check. Terminal is not permanent disposal and can still admit an explicit restart.
callGuard.name: Registration name. Invoke `beforeDispatch({ method, mode, generation })` before work: method is the remote path, generation is the actual supervisor generation, and mode is request, one-way, generator, async-generator or host-control; the example uses request.
A remote call guard.
inspect: Reads the current state of one registration by id. Use it when an application needs a point-in-time view without retaining the registration object. It returns undefined for an unknown id. The example above compares this view with registration.inspect().
inspect.id: Registration id.
An `IProcessResilienceSnapshot`, or `undefined`.
onTerminal: Subscribes to terminal entries reported by the actual supervisor and receives the registration snapshot. This observes the current terminal state rather than declaring the process permanently unrecoverable. The returned function removes this observer; call it during cleanup.
onTerminal.listener: Receives a registration snapshot and returns void or Promise<void>; one fulfilled handler marks this report handled and stops subsequent ticks. Rejection is reported. The returned unsubscribe is separate from closing governance.
An unsubscribe function.
close: Stops this failure-management object, closes listeners it owns and detaches its registrations. It does not own all resources involved in a connection: the accepting application still closes accepted endpoints and sessions, while the code that started execution still disposes its supervisor. The final cleanup block above shows these separate operations.
Resolves after owned governance resources close; it does not dispose caller-owned endpoints or supervisors.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
scheduler: Clock for rate windows, idle and drain timers.
Use the application-owned value shown here when configuring this connection. Omitted optional values keep their documented defaults.
report: Receives background errors that no call can reject with.
report.error: Original background failure value; preserve its source and code when present.
Nothing; the error is reported.
Send secondary failures to the application diagnostic sink while preserving the original error identity.
idempotencyStore: Store of results for `idempotencyKey` calls.
An in-memory store.
maxConnections: Connections accepted at once.
`64`.
maxConcurrentCallsPerConnection: Calls running at once per connection.
`32`.
maxCallsPerMinute: Calls per connection per minute.
`600`.
maxPayloadBytes: Largest payload accepted.
`16777216` (16 MiB).
maxConsecutiveTimeouts: Timeouts in a row that close the connection.
`3`.
idleTimeoutMs: Idle time after which a session closes.
`60000`.
drainMs: Time accepted calls get to finish when closing.
`5000`.
reportAtMs: When to report a terminal registration again (relative times).
`[0, 60000, 300000, 900000]`.
unhandledLimit: Unhandled terminal reports before liquidation starts.
liquidation: `{ cascade }`: also remove plugins depending on the liquidated one.
`cascade: false`: dependants are suspended.

symbols.purpose: Result of `peer.describe()`: this side identity, its methods and its connections.
symbols.core:
methods: Method paths provided by this local Peer; each connection detail separately lists its accepted remote methods.
counters: Call counters: `inFlight` (calls not yet finished) is measured; `sent`, `received`, `errors`, `lastActiveAt` are reported unavailable; or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
recent: Recent lifecycle records (`IRuntimeRecent`), newest last.
identity: Identity `{ name, instanceId }` of this Peer.
self: Same identity, as given by the `self` option or generated.
provide: Method paths this side provides.
connections: Details of every connection (`IRuntimeConnectionDetail`).
unit: Unavailable for a local Peer; see `connections`.
health: A local Peer may have several connections, so this field does not combine them into one health result. It returns an unavailable value. Inspect each connection to see whether that connection is healthy.
restartCount: Restart counts describe individual connections, not the local Peer as a whole. This field returns an unavailable value. Inspect the relevant connection when you need its restart count.
resources: Resource measurements belong to the execution unit behind each connection. The local Peer returns an unavailable value here rather than a combined measurement. Inspect a connection for the resource information its runtime supports.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
methods: Method paths provided by this local Peer; each connection detail separately lists its accepted remote methods.
counters: Call counters: `inFlight` (calls not yet finished) is measured; `sent`, `received`, `errors`, `lastActiveAt` are reported unavailable; or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
recent: Recent lifecycle records (`IRuntimeRecent`), newest last.
identity: Identity `{ name, instanceId }` of this Peer.
self: Same identity, as given by the `self` option or generated.
provide: Method paths this side provides.
connections: Details of every connection (`IRuntimeConnectionDetail`).
unit: Unavailable for a local Peer; see `connections`.
health: A local Peer may have several connections, so this field does not combine them into one health result. It returns an unavailable value. Inspect each connection to see whether that connection is healthy.
restartCount: Restart counts describe individual connections, not the local Peer as a whole. This field returns an unavailable value. Inspect the relevant connection when you need its restart count.
resources: Resource measurements belong to the execution unit behind each connection. The local Peer returns an unavailable value here rather than a combined measurement. Inspect a connection for the resource information its runtime supports.

self: Frozen local peer name and instanceId minted or supplied during this connection construction; it is not a remote authentication principal.
outcome: Queries the original remote operation ledger for a prior idempotency key, without dispatching that operation again.

describe: Queries the local accepted peer detail asynchronously. Without format returns IRuntimeDetail; json, yaml or toml returns the admitted text projection. It does not claim unavailable physical metrics.
describe.options: Optional query format from IRuntimeQueryOptions; omitted returns the object snapshot.

on: Registers a future RuntimeEventName listener after construction; factory resolution already represents initial readiness. Listener return is ignored and failures are contained by the runtime reporter.

on.listener: Callback receives IRuntimeEvent from this connection; return is ignored and throws or rejected thenables are reported.

close: Ends this logical connection and releases its owned channel resources; platform factories also terminate a worker or child they spawned.

sections.content: A Runtime Peer typed by `TRemote`: method names, payloads and results are checked against the other side API. Also has `self`, `describe()`, `outcome()`, `on()` and `close()`.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
self: Frozen local peer name and instanceId minted or supplied during this connection construction; it is not a remote authentication principal.
outcome: Queries the original remote operation ledger for a prior idempotency key, without dispatching that operation again.
outcome.idempotencyKey: The caller-issued key supplied as options.idempotencyKey on an earlier request to this connection.
Promise of IRpcRuntimeOutcomeResult; support and availability come from the accepted remote runtime contract.
describe: Queries the local accepted peer detail asynchronously. Without format returns IRuntimeDetail; json, yaml or toml returns the admitted text projection. It does not claim unavailable physical metrics.
describe.options: Optional query format from IRuntimeQueryOptions; omitted returns the object snapshot.
Promise of local detail or formatted text, following the selected query format.
on: Registers a future RuntimeEventName listener after construction; factory resolution already represents initial readiness. Listener return is ignored and failures are contained by the runtime reporter.
on.event: A RuntimeEventName value such as ready or exit; it selects future connection lifecycle notifications.
on.listener: Callback receives IRuntimeEvent from this connection; return is ignored and throws or rejected thenables are reported.
Idempotent removal function for this registration; closing the peer clears its publisher.
close: Ends this logical connection and releases its owned channel resources; platform factories also terminate a worker or child they spawned.
Shared completion Promise retaining the original close operation identity; no new calls are admitted once closing begins.
[Symbol.asyncDispose]: Scoped asynchronous cleanup is the exact original close operation, including its Promise identity.
The same completion Promise as close(), including platform-owned resource cleanup.
request: Calls a method the other side provides and waits for its result. Default deadline 30000 ms (`defaultTimeoutMs`); errors keep their native type and `(source, code)`.
request.method: Dotted path of a method in the other side `provide`, e.g. `math.double`.
request.args: `(payload?, options?)`: one payload and call options (`timeoutMs`, `signal`, `transfer`, `idempotencyKey`).
The method result, typed from `TRemote`.
notify: Sends a one-way call; no result comes back.
notify.method: Dotted method path provided by the other side.
notify.args: `(payload?, options?)` as for `request`.
Resolves once the call was sent.
stream: Calls a method that returns an iterable and yields its items as they arrive.
stream.method: Dotted path of an iterator method provided by the other side.
stream.args: `(payload?, options?)` as for `request`.
An async iterator of the yielded items.
group: Sends several calls as one batch and returns the outcome of each step in order.
group.steps: Steps `{ method, payload? }` in order.
group.options: Batch options such as `timeoutMs` and `signal`.
One outcome per step (success value or error).

blocks.text: Core 调用错误包括 DEADLINE_EXCEEDED/TimeoutError、CANCELLED/AbortError、OVERLOADED、PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND、TRANSPORT，Remote/PluginHost/Supervision 包装保持各自 source。业务原生 RangeError 等经 wire 还原原类型/message/stack/cause，不假装成 Process 主机错误。
自动来源失败先确认确由库 launcher 启动；握手超时确认先消费 bootstrap、stdin 正在读取、stdout 仅协议；socket 检查回环/权限/token。notify 只证明发送；大文件用业务分片/stream 或传约定路径由对端读取。Node 孙进程与强制终止限制、其它宿主权限/能力应按实际平台验证。

options: Optional `{ runtimeApiBootstrap }`: identity written to the child bootstrap; set by short sources automatically.
An `IProcessLauncher` from `@migaia/supervision/process`, used as `supervision.launcher`.
runtimeApiBootstrap: Advanced `IProcessRuntimeBootstrapOptions` from the owning Core source setup, supplying the process bootstrap context; normal short sources arrange it automatically.
Omitted: no explicit runtime bootstrap override is configured on this launcher.
Use the application-owned value shown here when configuring this connection. Omitted optional values keep their documented defaults.
runtimeApiBootstrap.name: Caller-selected child connection name; a held Core launch context supplies its childName or self.name before considering this override.
runtimeApiBootstrap.parentInstanceId: Parent Peer self.instanceId issued by the owning runtime; a held Core launch context supplies its own identity automatically.
runtimeApiBootstrap.generation: Supervision-issued IRpcRuntimeGeneration for this launch, preserving the original generation identity rather than a caller-invented counter.
Omitted: no explicit generation is written unless held Core launch context supplies one.
